title: Superannuation (Sustaining the Superannuation Contribution Concession) Imposition Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would impose an additional tax on specified superannuation contributions of very high income earners, alongside a companion bill establishing the assessment rules.
It would charge 15 per cent of taxable contributions under Division 293, with the companion rules covering relevant income and contributions above $300,000.
The package would cover contributions from 2012-13, while this imposition bill would limit the tax to circumstances within the Commonwealth's constitutional powers.
changes: A separate statutory charge would impose Division 293 tax on individuals with taxable contributions.
The rate of the charge would be fixed at 15 per cent.
An express safeguard would exclude any imposition beyond the Commonwealth's legislative power.
summary.affected: Individuals with taxable superannuation contributions under the Division 293 rules are affected.

speeches.speaker: Deb O'Neill
speeches.brief: Supported the superannuation bills, saying the $35,000 concessional cap will benefit 171,000 Australians over 60 from July and 363,000 aged over 50 from July 2014, and that the low-income superannuation contribution of up to $500 will help 3.6 million Australians earning under $37,000, including 2.1 million women.
